title: Create tiered entry criteria and deprecation signal for open models
creator: Sofia Patel
description:
Background: As we continue to accept community/open model submissions we need a lightweight, deterministic way to decide (a) whether a model can be ingested without a strict version pin, (b) what compatibility metadata must be supplied, and (c) how to surface an automated deprecation signal when upstream weights change or exhibit regressions. Current intake is inconsistent: some models land unpinned and later cause runtime incompatibilities; others are over-constrained and require manual engineering work to prove compatibility.

Goal: Define a tiered entry checklist (Tier 0..3) for open-model intake that maps to required metadata, automated runtime probes, and allowed pinning exemptions. Define a clear deprecation signal (catalog flag + webhook) and an automated rollback recommendation path for runtime-detected regressions. Produce a short PRD and acceptance criteria that engineering can implement as catalog ingestion validations and a runtime probe job.

Scope:
- In scope: entry tiers definition, required metadata fields per tier, runtime probe specification (sanity probes and latency profile), deprecation signal schema and webhook contract, intake UI/CLI validation messages, and rollout plan.
- Out of scope: implementation of kernel-level fixes, on-prem private deployment policies, and billing changes.

Trade-offs considered:
- Strict mandatory pinning reduces runtime regressions but increases maintenance and blocks rapid onboarding. Tiered approach aims to let low-risk experimental variants in with stricter probes while requiring production-grade models to pin.
- Automated deprecation signals could create noise for model authors; we'll include rate-limiting and a staged notification cadence.

Deliverables: PRD doc, JSON schema for deprecation webhook, intake validation rules, sample dashboard alerts for catalog console, and an engineering acceptance checklist.
acceptance_criteria: Define 4 entry tiers (0 experimental, 1 preview, 2 production-candidate, 3 certified) with 3-5 required metadata fields each.
Specify exact metadata fields: model_architecture, tokenizer_digest, supported_max_sequence, runtime_compatibility_tags, recommended_quantization_profiles.
Provide runtime probe spec: 50 sample prompts, latency/throughput target envelope per model size, and a regression detection heuristic (token accuracy drop + latency spike).

Deprecation signal defined as: catalog.flag = deprecated | unstable | ok; webhook payload JSON schema with model_key, observed_issue, first_seen, severity. Example payload and signing method included.
Intake UI shows tier recommendation and validation errors/warnings based on new rules; validation implemented as CLI exit codes 0/1/2 mapping to ok/warn/fail.
Engineering acceptance checklist with 6 items (schema validation, probe runner, webhook delivery, console flag, docs, end-to-end test) signed off by eng leads.
Create 3 sample onboarding cases in Confluence (experimental unpinned, preview pinned, certified pinned) with expected behavior and rollback guidance.
